newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed in weak trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed in weak trade.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed with a positive bias in thin trading on Wednesday following the shekel's decline against the dollar, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.19 percent, or 0.35 points, to 188.13 on low turnover of 43 million shekels against 53 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.29 percent to 198.61.
"Trading was mixed and the market was showing weakness. Activity is low and the only thing that affected trading today was the forex market," said a trader at Evergreen Capital Markets.

"During early trading the market rose following the shekel's decline, but when the shekel began to recover the market fell again. We are all waiting for the announcement on interest rates on Monday," she said.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2510 shekels against 3.2460 on Tuesday.
The central bank will announce interest rates for November on October 28. The key short-term rate is now 15.5 percent.

"Today's main story was the low turnover. Activity was so low that it was impossible to buy or sell. The market cannot recover with such low volume," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
"The weakening of the shekel had some impact on trading today. But, with such a low activity today's rise is meaningless," Nahum added.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which lost 1.5 percent to 28,830 on turnover of 4.0 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which fell 0.5 percent to 461 on volume of 2.7 million shekels; and Discount Investments which rose 3.0 percent to 18,555.
Traders said Discount's rise was only a technical correction following a sharp decline last week.
